newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court dismisses charges against ex-KGB agent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court dismisses charges against ex-KGB agent.

text.p: U.S. Magistrate Charles Swartwood accepted a motion on Thursday by federal prosecutors to dismiss all charges against a former Soviet KGB agent charged with conspiring to steal top secret information about the Star Wars defence programme.

The former agent, Vladimir Galkin, was accused of trying to obtain secret information from a Northborough, Mass., employee of Data General about the Strategic Defence Intiative or Star Wars programme in 1991.

Swartwood accepted the motion to dismiss made by Asst. U.S. Attorney Kevin Cloherty in a quick 15-minute proceeding. The written motion to dismiss said the action was taken "in the national interest."

Galkin's defense attorney told reporters while waiting for his client to be released by U.S. Marshals, "The government is not considering anything wrong with the evidence they had. They're dropping the charges for other reasons, because of other foreign policy decisions."
The 50-year-old former spy, who did not conceal his past occupation on a visa application, was arrested by FBI agents on Oct. 29 at John F. Kennedy airport in New York.
In Washington, the Justice Department said it had filed the motion to dismiss the criminal complaint against Galkin charging him with attempted espionage and conspiracy.
